newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pasminco says Century deal unchanged.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pasminco says Century deal unchanged.

text.p: Metals miner Pasminco Ltd said on Friday that the failure of talks between RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd and aborigines over the Century zinc mine did not threaten Pasminco's plans to eventually buy the project for A$345 million.
"We've told the market that we've allowed a period of arbitration as well so there's no change really," Pasminco spokeswoman Rell Hannah told Reuters.
She said the overnight failure of talks did not threaten the deal.

RTZ-CRA said early on Friday that talks with aboriginal groups over development of the massive Century zinc mine in the state of Queensland collapsed overnight. "We obviously are disappointed that the negotiations did not produce a result," a spokesman for RTZ-CRA subsidiary Century Zinc Ltd told Reuters.
Negotiations will now shift to the Federal native title tribunal where a binding agreement can take up to six months.

CRA and the Queensland government have withdrawn a A$60 million jobs and compensation package which was offered during the talks, said Rick Farley, the lead negotiator for the 12 aboriginal groups involved in the talks.
The company had set a deadline of Thursday midnight (1300 GMT) for agreement with the groups to proceed with development of the A$1 billion mine.
"The situation now is that only four out of the 12 claimants had signed the agreement by the midnight deadline," Farley said.
"Subsequently the company and the Queensland government have withdrawn their offer," he said.

It was still possible to reach an agreement in the next few days that could be presented to Century Zinc for approval, thus avoiding arbitration in the tribunal, Farley said. "That is possible but just how likely is another question," he said.
The talks were focused on land rights under Australia's Native Title legislation and over the A$60 million compensation and jobs package.
RTZ-CRA has said the deal to sell the Century project to Pasminco could collapse if the talks failed.

Pasminco, the world's biggest zinc producer, had earlier planned to buy half of the mine's annual output of 780,000 tonnes of low iron-bearing intermediate concentrates to feed its Budel zinc smelter in the Netherlands.
Century's development is crucial to the continued operation of the Budel smelter, whose current operating licence requires it to cease generating hazardous jarosite zinc residue.
If development work was to start on the mine in the next several months, production could commence in the latter part of the year 2000, Century Zinc said.
